authority: DD-80 decisions v1.88 · b0-auth-credential-lifecycle-design-probe.md §6 (session issuance/rotation) · feature_web_auth_onboarding_tech.md §4 Session Security (ENABLEMENT GATE callout, v2.11) · Verdict 10 accepted-residual-risk
blocks_enablement: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET must NOT be set in ANY environment until this slice is merged. Until then Google login stays fail-closed (503) and the residual risk below is not live.
problem_statement: A SameSite=Strict session cookie is NOT sent on the cross-site OAuth callback, so the callback cannot read, rotate or revoke a pre-existing session. D1 therefore mints fresh (matrix D1-2 + D1-13) and a pre-login session SURVIVES Google login without being invalidated — if an attacker knows that older token it stays valid. Capturing at /state and revoking at callback was tried and rejected in D1: it is non-atomic, races logout-all (a new P1 at round 06) and still misses when /state itself is entered cross-site.
intended_shape: Add a SAME-SITE completion hop after the cross-site callback lands, so the EXISTING issueSession() runs where the Strict cookie is present and takes its existing rotate branch. No new primitive: auth_rotate_web_session (0015) is already the atomic parent-locked epoch-revalidated swap proven by D0a barriers.
pinned_mechanism: M3 — the callback returns a first-party NON-MUTATING landing document that auto-submits a same-origin POST to the completion endpoint, with a <noscript> 'Continue' button as the no-JS fallback. MEASURED, not assumed: docs/probe-strict-cookie-completion-hop.md (2026-07-22) ran a two-site harness on Chromium 149, Firefox 151 and WebKit 26.5 — a bare 302 from the callback (M1) does NOT carry the Strict cookie on ANY of the three engines, while every mechanism that commits a first-party document first does. M3 was chosen over the equally-measured M2/M4/M5 because it reuses the two-hop pattern B0 §8 already uses for email verify/reset (one pattern, not two) and because POST carries an Origin header, so the existing sameOriginRequest() guard protects the mutating step independently of cookie semantics.
negative_scope: NO re-litigating the D1 mint-fresh contract (D1-2 session mint, D1-13 Strict) — this slice ADDS the hop, it does not change what D1 shipped
NO capture-at-state / revoke-at-callback workaround — already rejected in D1 as non-atomic and racing logout-all
NO new OAuth provider, no Facebook, no Telegram removal
NO weakening the Strict attribute on the session cookie to make rotation easier
handoff_persistence: OPEN IMPLEMENTATION CHOICE, decide and document before coding. With M3 the callback can no longer call issueSession(), so the account it resolved (route.ts:180 `login.accountId`, today consumed inline at :201) must reach the completion endpoint. auth_oauth_transactions (0017) has NO column for a resolved account. Two acceptable shapes: (a) MIGRATION — add expand-only columns to auth_oauth_transactions (e.g. resolved_account_id + handoff_hash + handoff_expires_at) as 0018, reusing the row's existing single-use/terminal machinery, and mirror in schema.ts; or (b) NO MIGRATION — carry a signed short-TTL handoff in a Lax cookie (a Lax cookie IS sent on a same-site POST) PROVIDED single-use is still enforced SERVER-SIDE against a durable fence, never by the signature alone. Whichever is chosen, D1B-5 (replay) and D1B-6 (expiry) must be satisfied by a server-side fence. If (a) is chosen, 0018 is expand-only and the migration tail moves 0017 -> 0018.
acceptance_obligation: Acceptance rows must be authored before this slice is CODE_READY (Verdict required). At minimum: (1) a pre-login session is revoked after a completed Google login via the same-site hop; (2) the rotation is atomic and does not race logout-all in either lock order; (3) an interrupted hop leaves NO half-state — either the old session survives intact or it is revoked and the new one is live, never both-dead; (4) the Strict attribute on the session cookie is unchanged; (5) Google login still fails closed when config is absent.
